name: VidSegNet
description: Single Object Segmentation Tracking (SOST) is a crucial task in computer vision with numerous real-world applications, such as video surveillance, sports performance evaluation, and medical analysis. Despite its importance, SOST faces several challenges, including object occlusion, interference from similar objects, and deformation. The newly created model or algorithms must be resilient to such difficult circumstances. To test this condition, a high-quality dataset is required. This paper introduces a new benchmark dataset specifically designed to address the future development of single object segmentation, focusing on real-world applications and challenges such as persis-tent tracking, occlusion, scale variation, and background clutter which contains 100 real-world videos. The dataset is trained and tested on three state-of-the-art algorithms: SiamMask, XMem, and Cuite, offering researchers essential metrics to bootstrap the advancement of their proposed methods in the field of SOST. The dataset can be found at: https://github.com/asfakalilVidSegNet.
evaluation_method: J&F (region similarity J and contour F) and mean IoU (intersection-over-union)
general_score_metric: J&F (mean of region similarity J and contour accuracy F)
reputation: New academic benchmark (2024) with limited but growing attention in the video segmentation and tracking communities.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; focuses on single-object video segmentation and tracking. Uses standard temporal segmentation metrics (J&F, IoU). May have dataset size/diversity limitations and annotation cost; low contamination risk.
